1	// This file pins down the decoder's handling of corrupted *internal list
2	// lengths*: archives whose outer framing, declared payload length and
3	// checksum are all correct, but where a count declared inside the payload
4	// cannot be satisfied by the bytes that follow. Three lists carry counts:
5	// the material's record list, a policy change's policy list, and the string
6	// lists used for subject roles and matched policies.
7	//
8	// Every corruption below is reframed with a consistent outer length and
9	// checksum, so exercising these cases proves the protection comes from
10	// decoding the payload's own structure rather than from the framing-level
11	// samples in audit_archive_test.go. A count the body cannot satisfy, a
12	// count word cut off mid-read, and a complete early item followed by an
13	// incomplete later item are all unreadable archives: DecodeAuditArchive
14	// must return ErrInvalidArchive (matched by errors.Is) and nil records,
15	// never a prefix and never a crash or hostile allocation.
16	package darksafe
17	
18	import (
19		"bytes"
20		"crypto/sha256"
21		"encoding/binary"
22		"errors"
23		"reflect"
24		"runtime"
25		"strings"
26		"testing"
27	)
28	
29	// listSite locates one length-counted list inside a payload, in payload
30	// byte offsets. itemEnds marks the byte just past each complete item.
31	type listSite struct {
32		markerAt int
33		countAt  int // -1 when the list is encoded nil
34		itemEnds []int
35	}
36	
37	// payloadInspector walks the known-good, two-record fixture payload in
38	// encode order. It exists only to locate the bytes a test corrupts; it
39	// mirrors archiveWriter, so a format change moves these tests off their
40	// target rather than silently corrupting the wrong field.
41	type payloadInspector struct {
42		b   []byte
43		pos int
44	}
45	
46	func (c *payloadInspector) u32() int {
47		v := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(c.b[c.pos : c.pos+4]))
48		c.pos += 4
49		return v
50	}
51	
52	func (c *payloadInspector) str() {
53		n := c.u32()
54		c.pos += n
55	}
56	
57	func (c *payloadInspector) marker() byte {
58		m := c.b[c.pos]
59		c.pos++
60		return m
61	}
62	
63	func (c *payloadInspector) stringListSite() listSite {
64		s := listSite{markerAt: c.pos, countAt: -1}
65		if c.marker() == archiveTagNil {
66			return s
67		}
68		s.countAt = c.pos
69		n := c.u32()
70		s.itemEnds = make([]int, 0, n)
71		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
72			c.str()
73			s.itemEnds = append(s.itemEnds, c.pos)
74		}
75		return s
76	}
77	
78	func (c *payloadInspector) policySite() {
79		c.str() // ID
80		c.str() // Subject
81		c.str() // Action
82		c.str() // Scope
83		c.str() // Effect
84		c.pos++ // Recursive bool
85		c.str() // ResourceID
86	}
87	
88	func (c *payloadInspector) policyListSite() listSite {
89		s := listSite{markerAt: c.pos, countAt: -1}
90		if c.marker() == archiveTagNil {
91			return s
92		}
93		s.countAt = c.pos
94		n := c.u32()
95		s.itemEnds = make([]int, 0, n)
96		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
97			c.policySite()
98			s.itemEnds = append(s.itemEnds, c.pos)
99		}
100		return s
101	}
102	
103	// inspectTwoRecordPayload locates the four counted lists in the fixture
104	// built by listCorruptionFixture.
105	func inspectTwoRecordPayload(t *testing.T, p []byte) fixtureSites {
106		t.Helper()
107		c := &payloadInspector{b: p}
108		c.str()    // embedded org
109		c.pos += 4 // embedded end sequence
110		c.str()    // embedded checkpoint fingerprint
111		records := listSite{countAt: c.pos}
112		n := c.u32() // record count
113		if n != 2 {
114			t.Fatalf("fixture record count = %d, want 2", n)
115		}
116	
117		// Record 1: policy change with two policies, absent decision.
118		c.str()    // org
119		c.pos += 4 // seq
120		c.str()    // kind
121		if m := c.marker(); m != archiveTagPresent {
122			t.Fatalf("record 1 change marker = %d, want present", m)
123		}
124		c.pos += 4 // change version
125		policies := c.policyListSite()
126		c.pos += 4 // source version
127		c.pos++    // rolled back bool
128		if m := c.marker(); m != archiveTagNil {
129			t.Fatalf("record 1 decision marker = %d, want nil", m)
130		}
131		c.str() // prev fingerprint
132		c.str() // own fingerprint
133		records.itemEnds = append(records.itemEnds, c.pos)
134	
135		// Record 2: decision with two roles and two matched policies.
136		c.str()    // org
137		c.pos += 4 // seq
138		c.str()    // kind
139		if m := c.marker(); m != archiveTagNil {
140			t.Fatalf("record 2 change marker = %d, want nil", m)
141		}
142		if m := c.marker(); m != archiveTagPresent {
143			t.Fatalf("record 2 decision marker = %d, want present", m)
144		}
145		c.str() // request SubjectOrg
146		c.str() // request ResourceOrg
147		c.str() // subject ID
148		c.str() // subject Kind
149		roles := c.stringListSite()
150		c.pos++ // subject disabled bool
151		c.str() // resource ID
152		c.str() // resource scope
153		c.str() // action
154		c.pos++ // decision allowed bool
155		c.str() // decision reason
156		matched := c.stringListSite()
157		c.pos += 4 // decision version
158		c.str()    // prev fingerprint
159		c.str()    // own fingerprint
160		records.itemEnds = append(records.itemEnds, c.pos)
161	
162		if c.pos != len(p) {
163			t.Fatalf("inspector ended at %d, payload length %d", c.pos, len(p))
164		}
165		if len(roles.itemEnds) != 2 || len(matched.itemEnds) != 2 || len(policies.itemEnds) != 2 {
166			t.Fatalf("fixture lists must each hold 2 items: policies=%d roles=%d matched=%d",
167				len(policies.itemEnds), len(roles.itemEnds), len(matched.itemEnds))
168		}
169		return fixtureSites{records: records, policies: policies, roles: roles, matched: matched}
170	}
171	
172	// fixtureSites are the four counted lists in the two-record fixture.
173	type fixtureSites struct {
174		records  listSite
175		policies listSite
176		roles    listSite
177		matched  listSite
178	}
179	
180	// framePayload wraps a (possibly corrupted) payload with correct outer
181	// framing, declared length and checksum, so the failure under test is
182	// always internal list decoding rather than framing.
183	func framePayload(payload []byte) []byte {
184		out := append([]byte(nil), archiveMagic...)
185		var lb [4]byte
186		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(lb[:], uint32(len(payload)))
187		out = append(out, lb[:]...)
188		out = append(out, payload...)
189		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
190		return append(out, sum[:]...)
191	}
192	
193	// payloadOf extracts a copy of one archive's payload.
194	func payloadOf(t *testing.T, archive []byte) []byte {
195		t.Helper()
196		magicLen := len(archiveMagic)
197		n := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(archive[magicLen : magicLen+4]))
198		return append([]byte(nil), archive[magicLen+4:magicLen+4+n]...)
199	}
200	
201	// listCorruptionFixture builds complete, valid material: one policy change
202	// carrying two policies followed by one decision whose subject has two
203	// roles and whose decision matched two policies. All four counted lists
204	// therefore hold real, multi-item content.
205	func listCorruptionFixture(t *testing.T) ([]byte, []AuditRecord, Checkpoint) {
206		t.Helper()
207		s := NewStore()
208		s.Publish("acme", 0, []Policy{
209			allowPolicy("p1", "u1", "read", "org/a", false),
210			allowPolicy("p2", "u1", "read", "org/a", false),
211		})
212		req := OrgRequest{
213			SubjectOrg:  "acme",
214			ResourceOrg: "acme",
215			Subject:     Subject{ID: "u1", Roles: []string{"role-a", "role-b"}},
216			Resource:    Resource{ID: "r1", Scope: "org/a"},
217			Action:      "read",
218		}
219		original := s.Decide("acme", req)
220		recs, cp, err := s.AuditExport("acme", 0)
221		if err != nil {
222			t.Fatal(err)
223		}
224		archive, err := EncodeAuditArchive("acme", recs, cp)
225		if err != nil {
226			t.Fatal(err)
227		}
228		got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(archive, "acme", cp)
229		if err != nil {
230			t.Fatalf("fixture must decode: %v", err)
231		}
232		review, err := RecheckDecisionOffline("acme", got, cp, 2)
233		if err != nil || !review.Consistent || !reflect.DeepEqual(review.Original, original) {
234			t.Fatalf("fixture review = %+v, %v", review, err)
235		}
236		return archive, recs, cp
237	}
238	
239	// TestArchiveInternalListCountCorruption covers, for every counted list,
240	// the shapes that make a payload unreadable: a declared count the
241	// remaining bytes cannot satisfy, a count word cut off mid-read, and a
242	// complete early item followed by a later item missing a required field.
243	// All arrive with valid outer framing and checksum and must be reported as
244	// ErrInvalidArchive with nil records — even when a complete, readable
245	// prefix (a full policy change and decision) precedes the damage.
246	func TestArchiveInternalListCountCorruption(t *testing.T) {
247		good, _, cp := listCorruptionFixture(t)
248		basePayload := payloadOf(t, good)
249		sites := inspectTwoRecordPayload(t, basePayload)
250	
251		// expectInvalid runs one payload mutation and asserts the whole read
252		// fails as an unreadable archive without delivering the intact prefix.
253		// It also proves the failed call rewrites neither its input bytes nor
254		// the retained checkpoint handed to it.
255		expectInvalid := func(name, wantSubstr string, mutate func(p []byte) []byte) {
256			t.Helper()
257			payload := mutate(append([]byte(nil), basePayload...))
258			data := framePayload(payload)
259			dataSnapshot := append([]byte(nil), data...)
260			cpSnapshot := cp
261	
262			got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(data, "acme", cp)
263			if !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidArchive) {
264				t.Fatalf("%s: err = %v, want ErrInvalidArchive", name, err)
265			}
266			if errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidRange) {
267				t.Fatalf("%s: structurally unreadable list counted as a content error: %v", name, err)
268			}
269			if got != nil {
270				t.Fatalf("%s: returned %d records on a damaged list, want nil", name, len(got))
271			}
272			if wantSubstr != "" && !strings.Contains(err.Error(), wantSubstr) {
273				t.Fatalf("%s: err = %q, want substring %q", name, err.Error(), wantSubstr)
274			}
275			if !bytes.Equal(data, dataSnapshot) {
276				t.Fatalf("%s: failed decode rewrote the archive bytes", name)
277			}
278			if cp != cpSnapshot {
279				t.Fatalf("%s: failed decode rewrote the checkpoint", name)
280			}
281		}
282	
283		lists := []struct {
284			name     string
285			site     listSite
286			minBytes int
287		}{
288			{"records", sites.records, 22},
289			{"policies", sites.policies, 6*4 + 1},
290			{"roles", sites.roles, 4},
291			{"matched", sites.matched, 4},
292		}
293	
294		for _, l := range lists {
295			// A) The count word is intact but promises more items than the bytes
296			// left could ever hold. Rewrite only the count (payload length
297			// unchanged): the read must fail as an unreadable archive, whether
298			// the per-item floor rejects the count up front or reading the
299			// missing items truncates — the error class is what the caller uses.
300			//
301			// This count value is the smallest one whose floor exceeds the
302			// remaining bytes, computed from this fixture's real offsets.
303			overCount := (len(basePayload)-(l.site.countAt+4))/l.minBytes + 1
304			expectInvalid(l.name+": count exceeds remaining items", "",
305				func(p []byte) []byte {
306					binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(p[l.site.countAt:], uint32(overCount))
307					return p
308				})
309	
310			// The maximum uint32 count on this small body must fail with the
311			// same deterministic error for every counted list, not just the
312			// record list, and without enumerating (or provisioning) the
313			// phantom items.
314			expectInvalid(l.name+": max uint32 count on small body", "implausible list count",
315				func(p []byte) []byte {
316					binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(p[l.site.countAt:], 0xffffffff)
317					return p
318				})
319	
320			// C) Every early item is whole; the final item is missing its last
321			// required field by one byte. Enough bytes remain to pass the coarse
322			// per-item count floor, so this failure must surface while reading
323			// that item — proving the item-level truncation guard, not only the
324			// count bound, is in place.
325			lastItemEnd := l.site.itemEnds[len(l.site.itemEnds)-1]
326			expectInvalid(l.name+": later item missing required field", "truncated archive payload",
327				func(p []byte) []byte { return p[:lastItemEnd-1] })
328		}

330		// B) A count word physically cut off mid-read. For the three inner
331		// lists this needs a one-record payload: the outer record-count floor
332		// (22 bytes per record) must still pass so the reader actually reaches
333		// the inner list and proves its own u32 truncation guard.
334		inner := buildInnerListCountTruncationPayloads(t)
335		cutCountWord := func(name string, full []byte, countAt int) {
336			t.Helper()
337			// These are single-record payloads, so the outer record-count floor
338			// (22 bytes/record) still passes at this cut; the reader must reach
339			// the inner list and prove its own count-word truncation guard.
340			cut := countAt + 2
341			data := framePayload(full[:cut])
342			got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(data, "acme", cp)
343			if !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidArchive) || got != nil {
344				t.Fatalf("%s: records=%v err=%v, want ErrInvalidArchive, nil", name, got, err)
345			}
346			if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "truncated archive payload") {
347				t.Fatalf("%s: err = %q, want a mid-read count truncation", name, err)
348			}
349		}
350		cutCountWord("policies count word", inner.policiesPayload, inner.policiesCountAt)
351		cutCountWord("roles count word", inner.rolesPayload, inner.rolesCountAt)
352		cutCountWord("matched count word", inner.matchedPayload, inner.matchedCountAt)
353	
354		// B for the outer record list: header complete, its count word cut.
355		headerOnly := buildArchiveHeader(t)
356		recordCountCut := append(append([]byte(nil), headerOnly...), 0x00, 0x00)
357		if got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(framePayload(recordCountCut), "acme", cp); !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidArchive) || got != nil {
358			t.Fatalf("records count word: records=%v err=%v, want ErrInvalidArchive, nil", got, err)
359		}
360	
361		// A dedicated emphasis for the requirement: a tiny archive declaring
362		// 4294967295 records must return the deterministic error promptly,
363		// without crashing or provisioning as if the count were real.
364		w := &archiveWriter{}
365		w.stringField("acme")
366		w.u32(0)
367		w.stringField("g")
368		w.u32(0xffffffff)
369		if w.err != nil {
370			t.Fatal(w.err)
371		}
372		tinyHuge := framePayload(w.buf)
373	
374		var before, after runtime.MemStats
375		runtime.GC()
376		runtime.ReadMemStats(&before)
377		got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(tinyHuge, "acme", cp)
378		runtime.ReadMemStats(&after)
379		if !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidArchive) || got != nil {
380			t.Fatalf("tiny archive with max count: records=%v err=%v, want ErrInvalidArchive, nil", got, err)
381		}
382		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "implausible list count") {
383			t.Fatalf("tiny archive with max count: err = %q, want count-bound rejection", err)
384		}
385		// A regression that trusted the count would try to provision billions
386		// of records; bound what this error path may allocate.
387		if alloc := after.TotalAlloc - before.TotalAlloc; alloc > 16<<20 {
388			t.Fatalf("max-count decode allocated %d bytes, want a small error path", alloc)
389		}
390	}

607			},

611				r.Subject.Roles = nil
612				return AuditDecision, nil, &DecisionRecord{
613					Request:  r,
614					Decision: Decision{Allowed: true, Reason: "matched allow policy", Matched: nil, Version: 3},
615				}
616			},
617			func(seq int) (string, *PolicyChange, *DecisionRecord) {
618				r := req
619				r.Subject.Roles = []string{}
620				return AuditDecision, nil, &DecisionRecord{
621					Request:  r,
622					Decision: Decision{Allowed: true, Reason: "matched allow policy", Matched: []string{}, Version: 3},
623				}
624			},
625			func(seq int) (string, *PolicyChange, *DecisionRecord) {
626				r := req
627				r.Subject.Roles = []string{"zeta", "alpha"} // order is preserved, not sorted
628				return AuditDecision, nil, &DecisionRecord{
629					Request: r,
630					Decision: Decision{Allowed: true, Reason: "matched allow policy",
631						Matched: []string{"p" + invalidByte, "p2"}, Version: 3},
632				}
633			},

641		if err != nil {

643		}

649		if got[0].Change.Policies != nil {

1	// This file is the single definition of which fields a Policy carries for
2	// every audit-side treatment of policy content: the fingerprint's raw
3	// canonical encoder, the valid-UTF-8 test that chooses between the JSON and
4	// raw fingerprint families, and the archive writer and reader. Each of
5	// those walks the one table below instead of naming the fields itself, so
6	// the fields and their order mean the same thing everywhere. Adding or
7	// changing a policy field here reaches fingerprinting, the UTF-8 decision,
8	// archiving and unarchiving at once; no audit path can keep a stale list of
9	// its own.
10	//
11	// The table order is part of the wire and fingerprint contract: it is the
12	// historical fingerprint field order, and the archive mirrors it field for
13	// field. Authorization itself (org.go) is intentionally not driven from
14	// this table.
15	package darksafe
16	
17	import "unicode/utf8"
18	
19	// policyFieldKind says how one Policy field participates in fingerprinting
20	// and archiving.
21	type policyFieldKind int
22	
23	const (
24		// policyFieldString is a string field written unconditionally by both
25		// the fingerprint encoder and the archive.
26		policyFieldString policyFieldKind = iota
27		// policyFieldOptionalString is a string field carried by the legacy JSON
28		// fingerprint family under an omitempty tag. The raw fingerprint encoder
29		// appends it only when non-empty, so empty values keep the exact legacy
30		// fingerprint bytes; the archive always writes it, including the empty
31		// value, so the field still round trips on its own.
32		policyFieldOptionalString
33		// policyFieldBool is a boolean field. It has no UTF-8 representation, so
34		// the valid-UTF-8 scan skips it while both encoders write it.
35		policyFieldBool
36	)
37	
38	// policyFieldSpec locates one Policy field. The string accessors are set for
39	// policyFieldString and policyFieldOptionalString; the bool accessors are
40	// set for policyFieldBool. A field appears in policyFields exactly once, and
41	// that entry is the only place its struct member is named.
42	type policyFieldSpec struct {
43		kind      policyFieldKind
44		getString func(Policy) string
45		setString func(*Policy, string)
46		getBool   func(Policy) bool
47		setBool   func(*Policy, bool)
48	}
49	
50	// policyFields lists every Policy field in fingerprint canonical order,
51	// which the archive reproduces exactly. Recursive (the sole boolean) sits
52	// between Effect and ResourceID exactly as it always has; ResourceID is the
53	// one field that is optional for fingerprints but always archived.
54	var policyFields = [...]policyFieldSpec{
55		{
56			kind:      policyFieldString,
57			getString: func(p Policy) string { return p.ID },
58			setString: func(p *Policy, s string) { p.ID = s },
59		},
60		{
61			kind:      policyFieldString,
62			getString: func(p Policy) string { return p.Subject },
63			setString: func(p *Policy, s string) { p.Subject = s },
64		},
65		{
66			kind:      policyFieldString,
67			getString: func(p Policy) string { return p.Action },
68			setString: func(p *Policy, s string) { p.Action = s },
69		},
70		{
71			kind:      policyFieldString,
72			getString: func(p Policy) string { return p.Scope },
73			setString: func(p *Policy, s string) { p.Scope = s },
74		},
75		{
76			kind:      policyFieldString,
77			getString: func(p Policy) string { return string(p.Effect) },
78			setString: func(p *Policy, s string) { p.Effect = Effect(s) },
79		},
80		{
81			kind:    policyFieldBool,
82			getBool: func(p Policy) bool { return p.Recursive },
83			setBool: func(p *Policy, v bool) { p.Recursive = v },
84		},
85		{
86			kind:      policyFieldOptionalString,
87			getString: func(p Policy) string { return p.ResourceID },
88			setString: func(p *Policy, s string) { p.ResourceID = s },
89		},
90	}
91	
92	// policyHasNonUTF8 reports whether any string field of p carries bytes that
93	// are not valid UTF-8. It ranges the single field table, so its idea of
94	// which policy strings the fingerprint protects can never diverge from the
95	// fields the encoders write. A boolean field cannot carry a raw byte and is
96	// skipped by kind rather than listed separately.
97	func policyHasNonUTF8(p Policy) bool {
98		for i := range policyFields {
99			f := &policyFields[i]
100			if f.kind == policyFieldBool {
101				continue
102			}
103			if !utf8.ValidString(f.getString(p)) {
104				return true
105			}
106		}
107		return false
108	}

1	// This file is the single definition of which fields a PolicyChange carries
2	// for every audit-side treatment of policy-change content: the fingerprint's
3	// raw canonical encoder, the valid-UTF-8 test that chooses between the JSON
4	// and raw fingerprint families, the archive writer and reader, and the
5	// detaching copy that keeps stored records independent of caller slices. Each
6	// of those walks the one table below instead of naming the fields itself, so
7	// the fields and their order mean the same thing everywhere. Adding or
8	// changing a policy-change field here reaches fingerprinting, the UTF-8
9	// decision, archiving, unarchiving and cloning at once; no audit path can
10	// keep a stale list of its own.
11	//
12	// The table order is part of the wire and fingerprint contract: it is the
13	// historical policy-change field order — the new version, the full policy
14	// set, the source version, then the rollback marker — and the archive
15	// mirrors it field for field. Publishing and rollback themselves (org.go)
16	// are intentionally not driven from this table.
17	package darksafe
18	
19	// changeFieldKind says how one PolicyChange field participates in
20	// fingerprinting and archiving.
21	type changeFieldKind int
22	
23	const (
24		// changeFieldInt is a non-negative integer field (a policy version
25		// number). It has no UTF-8 representation, so the valid-UTF-8 scan skips
26		// it while both encoders write it.
27		changeFieldInt changeFieldKind = iota
28		// changeFieldPolicyList is the full policy set of the new version. Its
29		// nil-versus-empty shape and element order are preserved explicitly by
30		// both encoders, and its policy strings are protected by the valid-UTF-8
31		// scan through the single policy field table.
32		changeFieldPolicyList
33		// changeFieldBool is a boolean field (the rollback marker). It has no
34		// UTF-8 representation either.
35		changeFieldBool
36	)
37	
38	// changeFieldSpec locates one PolicyChange field. The accessors used depend
39	// on the kind: integer fields use getInt/setInt, the policy list uses
40	// getPolicies/setPolicies and booleans getBool/setBool. A field appears in
41	// changeFields exactly once, and that entry is the only place its struct
42	// member is named.
43	type changeFieldSpec struct {
44		kind        changeFieldKind
45		getInt      func(*PolicyChange) int
46		setInt      func(*PolicyChange, int)
47		getPolicies func(*PolicyChange) []Policy
48		setPolicies func(*PolicyChange, []Policy)
49		getBool     func(*PolicyChange) bool
50		setBool     func(*PolicyChange, bool)
51	}
52	
53	// changeFields lists every PolicyChange field in fingerprint canonical
54	// order, which the archive reproduces exactly: Version, Policies,
55	// SourceVersion, RolledBack, exactly as the historical encoding placed them.
56	var changeFields = [...]changeFieldSpec{
57		{
58			kind:   changeFieldInt,
59			getInt: func(c *PolicyChange) int { return c.Version },
60			setInt: func(c *PolicyChange, v int) { c.Version = v },
61		},
62		{
63			kind:        changeFieldPolicyList,
64			getPolicies: func(c *PolicyChange) []Policy { return c.Policies },
65			setPolicies: func(c *PolicyChange, l []Policy) { c.Policies = l },
66		},
67		{
68			kind:   changeFieldInt,
69			getInt: func(c *PolicyChange) int { return c.SourceVersion },
70			setInt: func(c *PolicyChange, v int) { c.SourceVersion = v },
71		},
72		{
73			kind:    changeFieldBool,
74			getBool: func(c *PolicyChange) bool { return c.RolledBack },
75			setBool: func(c *PolicyChange, v bool) { c.RolledBack = v },
76		},
77	}
78	
79	// changeHasNonUTF8 reports whether any policy string the change carries
80	// holds bytes that are not valid UTF-8. It ranges the single field table, so
81	// its idea of which change content the fingerprint protects can never
82	// diverge from the fields the encoders write. Integer and boolean fields
83	// cannot carry a raw byte and are skipped by kind rather than listed
84	// separately; which strings inside one policy are protected remains decided
85	// by the single policy field table alone.
86	func changeHasNonUTF8(c *PolicyChange) bool {
87		for i := range changeFields {
88			f := &changeFields[i]
89			if f.kind != changeFieldPolicyList {
90				continue
91			}
92			for _, p := range f.getPolicies(c) {
93				if policyHasNonUTF8(p) {
94					return true
95				}
96			}
97		}
98		return false
99	}
100	
101	// cloneChangeLists detaches every policy list field of src into dst,
102	// preserving each list's nil-versus-empty shape exactly as clonePolicies
103	// defines it. It ranges the single field table, so a policy list added to
104	// the payload is detached here without this function changing.
105	func cloneChangeLists(dst, src *PolicyChange) {
106		for i := range changeFields {
107			f := &changeFields[i]
108			if f.kind == changeFieldPolicyList {
109				f.setPolicies(dst, clonePolicies(f.getPolicies(src)))
110			}
111		}
112	}

1	// This file is the single definition of which fields a DecisionRecord
2	// carries for every audit-side treatment of decision content: the
3	// fingerprint's raw canonical encoder, the valid-UTF-8 test that chooses
4	// between the JSON and raw fingerprint families, the archive writer and
5	// reader, and the detaching copy that keeps stored records independent of
6	// caller slices. Each of those walks the one table below instead of naming
7	// the fields itself, so the fields and their order mean the same thing
8	// everywhere. Adding or changing a decision field here reaches
9	// fingerprinting, the UTF-8 decision, archiving, unarchiving and cloning at
10	// once; no audit path can keep a stale list of its own.
11	//
12	// The table order is part of the wire and fingerprint contract: it is the
13	// historical decision field order — the two organization names, the subject,
14	// the resource, the action, then the decision itself — and the archive
15	// mirrors it field for field. Authorization itself (org.go) is intentionally
16	// not driven from this table: Roles participates here as a saved request
17	// field even though org policy evaluation never matches on it.
18	package darksafe
19	
20	import "unicode/utf8"
21	
22	// decisionFieldKind says how one DecisionRecord field participates in
23	// fingerprinting and archiving.
24	type decisionFieldKind int
25	
26	const (
27		// decisionFieldString is a string field written from its exact bytes by
28		// both the fingerprint encoder and the archive.
29		decisionFieldString decisionFieldKind = iota
30		// decisionFieldStringList is a string slice whose nil-versus-empty
31		// shape and element order are preserved explicitly by both encoders.
32		decisionFieldStringList
33		// decisionFieldBool is a boolean field. It has no UTF-8 representation,
34		// so the valid-UTF-8 scan skips it while both encoders write it.
35		decisionFieldBool
36		// decisionFieldInt is a non-negative integer field (the policy version
37		// the decision used). It has no UTF-8 representation either.
38		decisionFieldInt
39	)
40	
41	// decisionFieldSpec locates one DecisionRecord leaf field. The accessors
42	// used depend on the kind: string fields use getString/setString, list
43	// fields getList/setList, booleans getBool/setBool and integers
44	// getInt/setInt. A field appears in decisionFields exactly once, and that
45	// entry is the only place its struct member is named.
46	type decisionFieldSpec struct {
47		kind decisionFieldKind
48		// groupTag, when non-zero, is a nesting marker the fingerprint encoder
49		// emits immediately before this field, opening the subject, resource or
50		// decision group exactly where the historical encoding placed it. The
51		// archive has no group markers and ignores this.
52		groupTag  fingerprintTag
53		getString func(*DecisionRecord) string
54		setString func(*DecisionRecord, string)
55		getList   func(*DecisionRecord) []string
56		setList   func(*DecisionRecord, []string)
57		getBool   func(*DecisionRecord) bool
58		setBool   func(*DecisionRecord, bool)
59		getInt    func(*DecisionRecord) int
60		setInt    func(*DecisionRecord, int)
61	}
62	
63	// decisionFields lists every DecisionRecord leaf field in fingerprint
64	// canonical order, which the archive reproduces exactly. The subject group
65	// opens at Subject.ID, the resource group at Resource.ID and the decision
66	// group at Decision.Allowed, matching the historical nesting markers.
67	var decisionFields = [...]decisionFieldSpec{
68		{
69			kind:      decisionFieldString,
70			getString: func(d *DecisionRecord) string { return d.Request.SubjectOrg },
71			setString: func(d *DecisionRecord, s string) { d.Request.SubjectOrg = s },
72		},
73		{
74			kind:      decisionFieldString,
75			getString: func(d *DecisionRecord) string { return d.Request.ResourceOrg },
76			setString: func(d *DecisionRecord, s string) { d.Request.ResourceOrg = s },
77		},
78		{
79			kind:      decisionFieldString,
80			groupTag:  tagSubject,
81			getString: func(d *DecisionRecord) string { return d.Request.Subject.ID },
82			setString: func(d *DecisionRecord, s string) { d.Request.Subject.ID = s },
83		},
84		{
85			kind:      decisionFieldString,
86			getString: func(d *DecisionRecord) string { return d.Request.Subject.Kind },
87			setString: func(d *DecisionRecord, s string) { d.Request.Subject.Kind = s },
88		},
89		{
90			kind:    decisionFieldStringList,
91			getList: func(d *DecisionRecord) []string { return d.Request.Subject.Roles },
92			setList: func(d *DecisionRecord, l []string) { d.Request.Subject.Roles = l },
93		},
94		{
95			kind:    decisionFieldBool,
96			getBool: func(d *DecisionRecord) bool { return d.Request.Subject.Disabled },
97			setBool: func(d *DecisionRecord, v bool) { d.Request.Subject.Disabled = v },
98		},
99		{
100			kind:      decisionFieldString,
101			groupTag:  tagResource,
102			getString: func(d *DecisionRecord) string { return d.Request.Resource.ID },
103			setString: func(d *DecisionRecord, s string) { d.Request.Resource.ID = s },
104		},
105		{
106			kind:      decisionFieldString,
107			getString: func(d *DecisionRecord) string { return d.Request.Resource.Scope },
108			setString: func(d *DecisionRecord, s string) { d.Request.Resource.Scope = s },
109		},
110		{
111			kind:      decisionFieldString,
112			getString: func(d *DecisionRecord) string { return d.Request.Action },
113			setString: func(d *DecisionRecord, s string) { d.Request.Action = s },
114		},
115		{
116			kind:     decisionFieldBool,
117			groupTag: tagDecision,
118			getBool:  func(d *DecisionRecord) bool { return d.Decision.Allowed },
119			setBool:  func(d *DecisionRecord, v bool) { d.Decision.Allowed = v },
120		},
121		{
122			kind:      decisionFieldString,
123			getString: func(d *DecisionRecord) string { return d.Decision.Reason },
124			setString: func(d *DecisionRecord, s string) { d.Decision.Reason = s },
125		},
126		{
127			kind:    decisionFieldStringList,
128			getList: func(d *DecisionRecord) []string { return d.Decision.Matched },
129			setList: func(d *DecisionRecord, l []string) { d.Decision.Matched = l },
130		},
131		{
132			kind:   decisionFieldInt,
133			getInt: func(d *DecisionRecord) int { return d.Decision.Version },
134			setInt: func(d *DecisionRecord, v int) { d.Decision.Version = v },
135		},
136	}
137	
138	// decisionRecordHasNonUTF8 reports whether any string or list element of d
139	// carries bytes that are not valid UTF-8. It ranges the single field table,
140	// so its idea of which decision strings the fingerprint protects can never
141	// diverge from the fields the encoders write. Boolean and integer fields
142	// cannot carry a raw byte and are skipped by kind rather than listed
143	// separately.
144	func decisionRecordHasNonUTF8(d *DecisionRecord) bool {
145		for i := range decisionFields {
146			f := &decisionFields[i]
147			switch f.kind {
148			case decisionFieldString:
149				if !utf8.ValidString(f.getString(d)) {
150					return true
151				}
152			case decisionFieldStringList:
153				for _, s := range f.getList(d) {
154					if !utf8.ValidString(s) {
155						return true
156					}
157				}
158			}
159		}
160		return false
161	}
162	
163	// cloneDecisionLists detaches every string list field of src into dst,
164	// preserving each list's nil-versus-empty shape. It ranges the single field
165	// table, so a list field added to the record is detached here without this
166	// function changing.
167	func cloneDecisionLists(dst, src *DecisionRecord) {
168		for i := range decisionFields {
169			f := &decisionFields[i]
170			if f.kind == decisionFieldStringList {
171				f.setList(dst, cloneStrings(f.getList(src)))
172			}
173		}
174	}

1	// This file implements the organization-scoped audit chain. Every successful
2	// policy publish or rollback, and every Decide called with a non-empty
3	// decision organization, leaves an immutable record in that organization.
4	//
5	// Records carry an organization-local sequence starting at 1 and a SHA-256
6	// fingerprint that chains each record to the previous one. The genesis
7	// fingerprint binds the organization name, so records from another
8	// organization can never validate as part of this chain even when the
9	// sequence numbers and identifiers coincide.
10	package darksafe
11	
12	import (
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/binary"
15		"encoding/hex"
16		"encoding/json"
17		"errors"
18		"fmt"
19		"unicode/utf8"
20	)
21	
22	// Audit record categories.
23	const (
24		// AuditPolicyChange is a successful publish or rollback.
25		AuditPolicyChange = "policy_change"
26		// AuditDecision is one Decide evaluation.
27		AuditDecision = "decision"
28	)
29	
30	// Sentinel errors for the audit entry points. Callers distinguish them
31	// with errors.Is; every one leaves state unchanged.
32	var (
33		// ErrInvalidPage means a page size or range argument was invalid.
34		ErrInvalidPage = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit page")
35		// ErrInvalidRange means the upper bound is beyond what exists, the
36		// range is inverted, or a supplied fingerprint does not match.
37		ErrInvalidRange = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit range")
38		// ErrAuditNotFound means no record exists at the requested sequence.
39		ErrAuditNotFound = errors.New("darksafe: audit record not found")
40		// ErrAuditNotADecision means the record at the sequence is not a
41		// decision record and therefore cannot be rechecked.
42		ErrAuditNotADecision = errors.New("darksafe: audit record is not a decision")
43	)
44	
45	// PolicyChange captures a successful publish or rollback.
46	type PolicyChange struct {
47		// Version is the newly created policy version.
48		Version int
49		// Policies is the full policy set of the new version.
50		Policies []Policy
51		// SourceVersion is the version copied by a rollback, and 0 for an
52		// ordinary publish.
53		SourceVersion int
54		// RolledBack reports whether the change was produced by Rollback.
55		RolledBack bool
56	}
57	
58	// DecisionRecord captures one Decide call: the full request and the
59	// decision actually returned.
60	type DecisionRecord struct {
61		Request  OrgRequest
62		Decision Decision
63	}
64	
65	// AuditRecord is one immutable entry in an organization's audit chain.
66	type AuditRecord struct {
67		Org      string
68		Seq      int // organization-local, starting at 1 and gapless
69		Kind     string
70		Change   *PolicyChange   // present when Kind == AuditPolicyChange
71		Decision *DecisionRecord // present when Kind == AuditDecision
72	
73		// PrevFingerprint is the fingerprint of the preceding record, or the
74		// genesis fingerprint for the first record.
75		PrevFingerprint string
76		// Fingerprint binds this record's full content to its predecessor.
77		Fingerprint string
78	}
79	
80	// hashEnvelope is the canonical, organization-bound representation that
81	// fingerprints are computed over. It is never exposed, so callers cannot
82	// forge one by constructing an AuditRecord with copied fields.
83	type hashEnvelope struct {
84		Org             string          `json:"org"`
85		Seq             int             `json:"seq"`
86		Kind            string          `json:"kind"`
87		Change          *PolicyChange   `json:"change,omitempty"`
88		Decision        *DecisionRecord `json:"decision,omitempty"`
89		PrevFingerprint string          `json:"prev"`
90	}
91	
92	// envelopeUsesRawBytes reports whether any string protected by the
93	// fingerprint carries bytes that are not valid UTF-8. Such envelopes are
94	// hashed through encodeCanonical instead of encoding/json, because JSON
95	// string encoding replaces invalid bytes with U+FFFD and would let two
96	// different raw contents share a fingerprint.
97	func envelopeUsesRawBytes(env *hashEnvelope) bool {
98		if !utf8.ValidString(env.Org) || !utf8.ValidString(env.Kind) ||
99			!utf8.ValidString(env.PrevFingerprint) {
100			return true
101		}
102		if env.Change != nil {
103			// Which change content is protected is decided by the single
104			// policy-change field table (change_fields.go), shared with the
105			// encoder, the archive and the detaching copy, rather than named here
106			// a second time; the policy strings inside it remain governed by the
107			// single policy field table.
108			if changeHasNonUTF8(env.Change) {
109				return true
110			}
111		}
112		if env.Decision != nil {
113			// Which decision strings are protected is decided by the single
114			// decision field table (decision_fields.go), shared with the encoder
115			// and the archive, rather than named here a second time.
116			if decisionRecordHasNonUTF8(env.Decision) {
117				return true
118			}
119		}
120		return false
121	}
122	
123	// rawEnvelopePrefix opens every raw-byte canonical encoding. It never
124	// coincides with the start of a JSON envelope (always '{'), so
125	// fingerprints from the two encodings live in collision-free spaces.
126	const rawEnvelopePrefix = "darksafe-audit-raw-v1\x00"
127	
128	// fingerprintTag delimits one field or nested value within the canonical
129	// binary encoding. Distinct tags keep two payloads that merely share
130	// adjacent bytes apart (e.g. ["ab",""] vs ["a","b"]).
131	type fingerprintTag byte
132	
133	const (
134		tagEnvelope fingerprintTag = iota + 1
135		tagSeq
136		tagString
137		tagStringList
138		tagBool
139		tagPolicy
140		tagPolicyList
141		tagChange
142		tagSubject
143		tagResource
144		tagDecision
145		tagDecisionRecord
146	)
147	
148	// fingerprintEncoder builds the canonical byte representation of an
149	// envelope. Unlike encoding/json it writes string contents byte-for-byte
150	// with an explicit length prefix, so strings carrying invalid UTF-8 stay
151	// distinguishable: encoding/json renders both a raw 0xFF byte and a raw
152	// 0xFE byte as the U+FFFD replacement rune, collapsing genuinely
153	// different content onto identical fingerprints.
154	type fingerprintEncoder struct {
155		buf []byte
156	}
157	
158	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) tag(t fingerprintTag) {
159		e.buf = append(e.buf, byte(t))
160	}
161	
162	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) int64Tag(t fingerprintTag, v int64) {
163		e.tag(t)
164		var b [8]byte
165		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(b[:], uint64(v))
166		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
167	}
168	
169	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) boolTag(t fingerprintTag, v bool) {
170		e.tag(t)
171		if v {
172			e.buf = append(e.buf, 1)
173		} else {
174			e.buf = append(e.buf, 0)
175		}
176	}
177	
178	// rawString tags and writes a string from its exact memory bytes. No
179	// validation, replacement or normalization is ever performed: an invalid
180	// UTF-8 byte reaches the hash unchanged.
181	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) rawString(s string) {
182		e.tag(tagString)
183		var b [4]byte
184		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(len(s)))
185		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
186		e.buf = append(e.buf, s...)
187	}
188	
189	// stringList preserves nil-vs-empty explicitly: in the JSON envelope a
190	// nil slice is "null" and a non-nil empty slice is "[]", so the raw
191	// encoding must keep the two shapes apart as well.
192	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) stringList(items []string) {
193		e.tag(tagStringList)
194		if items == nil {
195			e.buf = append(e.buf, 0)
196			return
197		}
198		e.buf = append(e.buf, 1)
199		var b [4]byte
200		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(len(items)))
201		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
202		for _, s := range items {
203			e.rawString(s)
204		}
205	}
206	
207	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) policy(p Policy) {
208		e.tag(tagPolicy)
209		// Field order, the Recursive boolean's position, and ResourceID being
210		// appended only when set all come from the single policy field table, so
211		// the fingerprint and the archive enumerate fields in exactly one place.
212		for i := range policyFields {
213			f := &policyFields[i]
214			switch f.kind {
215			case policyFieldString:
216				e.rawString(f.getString(p))
217			case policyFieldOptionalString:
218				// ResourceID participates only when set, pairing with its
219				// omitempty JSON tag, so the legacy fingerprint bytes are
220				// unchanged for resource-unrestricted policies.
221				if v := f.getString(p); v != "" {
222					e.rawString(v)
223				}
224			case policyFieldBool:
225				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(p))
226			}
227		}
228	}
229	
230	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) policyList(policies []Policy) {
231		e.tag(tagPolicyList)
232		if policies == nil {
233			e.buf = append(e.buf, 0)
234			return
235		}
236		e.buf = append(e.buf, 1)
237		var b [4]byte
238		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(len(policies)))
239		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
240		for _, p := range policies {
241			e.policy(p)
242		}
243	}
244	
245	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) change(c *PolicyChange) {
246		e.tag(tagChange)
247		// A nil pointer is encoded as tagChange alone; a present value's
248		// fields follow immediately.
249		if c == nil {
250			return
251		}
252		// Field order comes from the single policy-change field table, so the
253		// fingerprint, the UTF-8 decision, the archive and the detaching copy
254		// enumerate fields in exactly one place. No change field is skipped.
255		for i := range changeFields {
256			f := &changeFields[i]
257			switch f.kind {
258			case changeFieldInt:
259				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(c)))
260			case changeFieldPolicyList:
261				e.policyList(f.getPolicies(c))
262			case changeFieldBool:
263				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(c))
264			}
265		}
266	}

268	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) decisionRecord(d *DecisionRecord) {
269		e.tag(tagDecisionRecord)
270		if d == nil {
271			return
272		}
273		// Field order and the subject/resource/decision group markers all come
274		// from the single decision field table, so the fingerprint, the UTF-8
275		// decision and the archive enumerate fields in exactly one place. No
276		// request or decision field is skipped.
277		for i := range decisionFields {
278			f := &decisionFields[i]
279			if f.groupTag != 0 {
280				e.tag(f.groupTag)
281			}
282			switch f.kind {
283			case decisionFieldString:
284				e.rawString(f.getString(d))
285			case decisionFieldStringList:
286				e.stringList(f.getList(d))
287			case decisionFieldBool:
288				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(d))
289			case decisionFieldInt:
290				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(d)))
291			}
292		}
293	}

295	// encodeCanonical returns the raw bytes fingerprinted for an envelope
296	// whose strings include invalid UTF-8. Every string the record carries
297	// reaches the output byte-for-byte, at whatever nesting depth or list
298	// position it occupies. The prefix separates this encoding space from
299	// JSON fingerprints.
300	func encodeCanonical(env *hashEnvelope) []byte {
301		e := &fingerprintEncoder{buf: []byte(rawEnvelopePrefix)}
302		e.tag(tagEnvelope)
303		e.rawString(env.Org)
304		e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(env.Seq))
305		e.rawString(env.Kind)
306		e.change(env.Change)
307		e.decisionRecord(env.Decision)
308		e.rawString(env.PrevFingerprint)
309		return e.buf
310	}

312	// genesisFingerprint derives the chain root from the organization name,
313	// keeping equal identifiers in different organizations independent.
314	func genesisFingerprint(org string) string {
315		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte("darksafe-audit-genesis\x00" + org))
316		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
317	}
318	
319	// computeFingerprint returns the fingerprint for an envelope. Records made
320	// exclusively of valid UTF-8 keep the historical JSON fingerprint, so old
321	// exports and checkpoints remain valid; records containing invalid bytes
322	// use the length-prefixed raw encoding that protects their exact bytes.
323	func computeFingerprint(env *hashEnvelope) string {
324		if envelopeUsesRawBytes(env) {
325			sum := sha256.Sum256(encodeCanonical(env))
326			return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
327		}
328		b, err := json.Marshal(env)
329		if err != nil {
330			// All envelope fields are plain, JSON-encodable values; a failure
331			// here indicates a programming error, not user input.
332			panic(fmt.Errorf("darksafe: audit envelope must encode: %w", err))
333		}
334		sum := sha256.Sum256(b)
335		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
336	}
337	
338	// fingerprintFor builds and fingerprints the envelope for a record.
339	func fingerprintFor(r *AuditRecord) string {
340		return computeFingerprint(&hashEnvelope{
341			Org:             r.Org,
342			Seq:             r.Seq,
343			Kind:            r.Kind,
344			Change:          r.Change,
345			Decision:        r.Decision,
346			PrevFingerprint: r.PrevFingerprint,
347		})
348	}

350	// clonePolicies returns a detached copy of a policy set.
351	func clonePolicies(in []Policy) []Policy {
352		if in == nil {
353			return nil
354		}
355		return append([]Policy(nil), in...)
356	}
357	
358	// cloneChange returns a detached copy of a policy-change payload.
359	func cloneChange(c *PolicyChange) *PolicyChange {
360		if c == nil {
361			return nil
362		}
363		cp := *c
364		// Detach every list the single policy-change field table carries; the
365		// per-list nil-versus-empty handling stays exactly as clonePolicies
366		// defines it.
367		cloneChangeLists(&cp, c)
368		return &cp
369	}
370	
371	// cloneStrings returns a detached copy of a string slice while preserving
372	// its nil-versus-empty shape: a nil slice stays nil, and every non-nil
373	// slice, including a non-nil empty slice that still carries spare capacity,
374	// receives its own backing array. Copying only when len > 0 is not enough:
375	// a caller may submit make([]string, 0, 4), and aliasing that array into a
376	// stored record would let an append to one handed-out copy overwrite the
377	// first element of every other copy that shares it.
378	func cloneStrings(in []string) []string {
379		if in == nil {
380			return nil
381		}
382		return append([]string{}, in...)
383	}
384	
385	// cloneDecision returns a detached copy of a decision payload.
386	func cloneDecision(d *DecisionRecord) *DecisionRecord {
387		if d == nil {
388			return nil
389		}
390		cp := *d
391		// Detach every list the single decision field table carries, on non-nil
392		// rather than on len > 0 so empty-but-capacious lists are independent
393		// copies too; nil lists stay nil.
394		cloneDecisionLists(&cp, d)
395		return &cp
396	}
397	
398	// cloneRecord returns a fully detached copy of a record.
399	func cloneRecord(r *AuditRecord) *AuditRecord {
400		cp := *r
401		cp.Change = cloneChange(r.Change)
402		cp.Decision = cloneDecision(r.Decision)
403		return &cp
404	}
405	
406	// appendAuditLocked validates, fingerprints and stores one record. It runs
407	// under the store mutex and is the single place records are created.
408	func (st *orgState) appendAuditLocked(org, kind string, change *PolicyChange, decision *DecisionRecord) *AuditRecord {
409		seq := len(st.audit) + 1
410		prev := genesisFingerprint(org)
411		if len(st.audit) > 0 {
412			prev = st.audit[len(st.audit)-1].Fingerprint
413		}
414		// Store detached copies; later caller mutation must not reach the chain.
415		rec := &AuditRecord{
416			Org:             org,
417			Seq:             seq,
418			Kind:            kind,
419			Change:          cloneChange(change),
420			Decision:        cloneDecision(decision),
421			PrevFingerprint: prev,
422		}
423		rec.Fingerprint = fingerprintFor(rec)
424		st.audit = append(st.audit, rec)
425		return cloneRecord(rec)
426	}
427	
428	// auditHeadLocked returns the highest sequence in the chain and the
429	// fingerprint that covers it: (0, genesis) for an organization with no
430	// records.
431	func (st *orgState) auditHeadLocked(org string) (int, string) {
432		if len(st.audit) == 0 {
433			return 0, genesisFingerprint(org)
434		}
435		last := st.audit[len(st.audit)-1]
436		return last.Seq, last.Fingerprint
437	}
438	
439	// Checkpoint pins an audit query to an exact point in a chain.
440	type Checkpoint struct {
441		Org         string
442		EndSeq      int
443		Fingerprint string
444	}
445	
446	// AuditPage is one stable slice of an organization's audit chain.
447	type AuditPage struct {
448		Org     string
449		Records []AuditRecord
450		// BeginSeq/EndSeq delimit the whole pinned range, not just this page.
451		BeginSeq int
452		EndSeq   int
453		// Next is the first sequence of the following page, 0 when exhausted.
454		Next int
455		// Checkpoint is the pinned upper bound shared by every page.
456		Checkpoint Checkpoint
457	}
458	
459	// recordMatches reports whether a record survives the query filters.
460	func recordMatches(r *AuditRecord, kind, subjectID string) bool {
461		if kind != "" && r.Kind != kind {
462			return false
463		}
464		if subjectID != "" {
465			// A subject filter selects decision records of that subject only.
466			if r.Kind != AuditDecision || r.Decision == nil ||
467				r.Decision.Request.Subject.ID != subjectID {
468				return false
469			}
470		}
471		return true
472	}
473	
474	// AuditQuery pins the first page of an audit query. startSeq is the first
475	// sequence considered (1 from the beginning); endSeq <= 0 means "everything
476	// currently stored". The returned checkpoint must be passed to AuditPage
477	// for the following pages, so records appended after the first query never
478	// mix into later pages.
479	func (s *Store) AuditQuery(org string, startSeq, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string) (*AuditPage, error) {
480		if org == "" {
481			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
482		}
483		if kind != "" && kind != AuditPolicyChange && kind != AuditDecision {
484			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown category %q", ErrInvalidPage, kind)
485		}
486		if pageSize <= 0 {
487			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: page size must be positive, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, pageSize)
488		}
489		if startSeq < 1 {
490			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: start sequence must be >= 1, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, startSeq)
491		}
492		s.mu.Lock()
493		defer s.mu.Unlock()
494		st := s.orgLocked(org)
495		end, fingerprint := st.auditHeadLocked(org)
496		cp := Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: end, Fingerprint: fingerprint}
497		if end == 0 {
498			// An organization with no records always yields the empty genesis
499			// page, regardless of where the caller asked to begin.
500			return &AuditPage{Org: org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: 0, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
501		}
502		if startSeq > end {
503			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: start sequence %d is beyond end sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, startSeq, end)
504		}
505		return s.auditPageLocked(org, startSeq, end, fingerprint, pageSize, kind, subjectID), nil
506	}
507	
508	// AuditPage returns one page of a previously pinned query. nextSeq is the
509	// cursor from the previous page; when it is 0 the range is exhausted. The
510	// checkpoint is re-verified against the chain on every call.
511	func (s *Store) AuditPage(cp Checkpoint, nextSeq, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string) (*AuditPage, error) {
512		if cp.Org == "" {
513			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
514		}
515		if kind != "" && kind != AuditPolicyChange && kind != AuditDecision {
516			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown category %q", ErrInvalidPage, kind)
517		}
518		if pageSize <= 0 {
519			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: page size must be positive, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, pageSize)
520		}
521		if nextSeq < 0 {
522			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, nextSeq)
523		}
524		s.mu.Lock()
525		defer s.mu.Unlock()
526		st, ok := s.orgs[cp.Org]
527		if !ok {
528			// No organization state: the only valid checkpoint is an empty one.
529			g := genesisFingerprint(cp.Org)
530			if cp.EndSeq == 0 && cp.Fingerprint == g && nextSeq == 0 {
531				return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: 0, EndSeq: 0, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
532			}
533			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint organization has no records", ErrInvalidRange)
534		}
535		head := len(st.audit)
536		if cp.EndSeq < 0 || cp.EndSeq > head {
537			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq, head)
538		}
539		wantFP := genesisFingerprint(cp.Org)
540		if cp.EndSeq > 0 {
541			if cp.EndSeq > len(st.audit) {
542				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq, head)
543			}
544			wantFP = st.audit[cp.EndSeq-1].Fingerprint
545		}
546		if cp.Fingerprint != wantFP {
547			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint fingerprint does not match the chain at sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
548		}
549		if nextSeq == 0 {
550			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: cp.EndSeq, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
551		}
552		if nextSeq > cp.EndSeq+1 {
553			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence %d beyond pinned range ending at %d", ErrInvalidRange, nextSeq, cp.EndSeq)
554		}
555		if nextSeq == cp.EndSeq+1 {
556			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: nextSeq, EndSeq: cp.EndSeq, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
557		}
558		return s.auditPageLocked(cp.Org, nextSeq, cp.EndSeq, wantFP, pageSize, kind, subjectID), nil
559	}
560	
561	// auditPageLocked scans forward collecting up to pageSize matching records
562	// and computes the next-page cursor. It does not stop at pageSize raw
563	// records: filtering happens within the pinned [start,end] window.
564	func (s *Store) auditPageLocked(org string, startSeq, endSeq int, endFP string, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string) *AuditPage {
565		st := s.orgs[org]
566		// pageSize only bounds how many records this page returns; it must not
567		// drive allocation. A caller may pass any positive value, including the
568		// largest int, for a range holding a handful of records, so preallocate
569		// no more than the window can actually contain.
570		window := endSeq - startSeq + 1
571		capHint := pageSize
572		if window < capHint {
573			capHint = window
574		}
575		out := make([]AuditRecord, 0, capHint)
576		i := startSeq
577		for ; i <= endSeq && len(out) < pageSize; i++ {
578			r := st.audit[i-1]
579			if recordMatches(r, kind, subjectID) {
580				out = append(out, *cloneRecord(r))
581			}
582		}
583		next := 0
584		if i <= endSeq {
585			next = i
586		}
587		return &AuditPage{
588			Org:        org,
589			Records:    out,
590			BeginSeq:   startSeq,
591			EndSeq:     endSeq,
592			Next:       next,
593			Checkpoint: Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: endSeq, Fingerprint: endFP},
594		}
595	}
596	
597	// AuditExport returns detached copies of the complete records through
598	// endSeq, suitable for offline verification. endSeq <= 0 means everything
599	// currently stored. An organization with no records yields an empty slice
600	// together with its sequence-0 checkpoint.
601	func (s *Store) AuditExport(org string, endSeq int) (records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint, err error) {
602		if org == "" {
603			return nil, Checkpoint{}, ErrMissingOrganization
604		}
605		s.mu.Lock()
606		defer s.mu.Unlock()
607		st := s.orgLocked(org)
608		head := len(st.audit)
609		if endSeq <= 0 {
610			endSeq = head
611		}
612		if endSeq > head {
613			return nil, Checkpoint{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, endSeq, head)
614		}
615		if endSeq < 0 {
616			return nil, Checkpoint{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, endSeq)
617		}
618		// The checkpoint fingerprints the final exported record, not the
619		// possibly later current head.
620		fingerprint := genesisFingerprint(org)
621		if endSeq > 0 {
622			fingerprint = st.audit[endSeq-1].Fingerprint
623		}
624		out := make([]AuditRecord, 0, endSeq)
625		for i := 0; i < endSeq; i++ {
626			out = append(out, *cloneRecord(st.audit[i]))
627		}
628		return out, Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: endSeq, Fingerprint: fingerprint}, nil
629	}
630	
631	// VerifyAudit validates an exported record set entirely without a Store.
632	// The caller separately retains the organization, end sequence and
633	// fingerprint they expect. It rejects any modified field, missing middle or
634	// tail record, swapped order, and record spliced in from another
635	// organization. Empty or nil records validate exactly when the checkpoint
636	// is the organization's genesis (end sequence 0).
637	func VerifyAudit(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) error {
638		if org == "" {
639			return ErrMissingOrganization
640		}
641		if cp.Org != "" && cp.Org != org {
642			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint organization %q does not match %q", ErrInvalidRange, cp.Org, org)
643		}
644		genesis := genesisFingerprint(org)
645		if len(records) == 0 {
646			if cp.EndSeq != 0 || cp.Fingerprint != genesis {
647				return fmt.Errorf("%w: empty records but checkpoint claims end sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
648			}
649			return nil
650		}
651		if cp.EndSeq != len(records) {
652			return fmt.Errorf("%w: have %d records, checkpoint ends at %d", ErrInvalidRange, len(records), cp.EndSeq)
653		}
654		prev := genesis
655		for i, r := range records {
656			wantSeq := i + 1
657			if r.Org != org {
658				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d belongs to organization %q", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Org)
659			}
660			if r.Seq != wantSeq {
661				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d has sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Seq)
662			}
663			if r.PrevFingerprint != prev {
664				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d breaks the chain", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
665			}
666			wantFP := fingerprintFor(&r)
667			if r.Fingerprint != wantFP {
668				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d fingerprint mismatch", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
669			}
670			if r.Kind == AuditPolicyChange {
671				if r.Change == nil || r.Decision != nil {
672					return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d payload does not match its category", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
673				}
674			} else if r.Kind == AuditDecision {
675				if r.Decision == nil || r.Change != nil {
676					return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d payload does not match its category", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
677				}
678			} else {
679				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d has unknown category %q", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Kind)
680			}
681			prev = r.Fingerprint
682		}
683		last := records[len(records)-1]
684		if last.Fingerprint != cp.Fingerprint {
685			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint fingerprint does not match the final record", ErrInvalidRange)
686		}
687		return nil
688	}
689	
690	// RecheckDecision re-evaluates the request stored in an organization's
691	// decision record against the policy version that decision actually used.
692	// Later publishes or rollbacks cannot alter the result. Non-decision
693	// records and missing sequences return distinguishable errors.
694	//
695	// The record and the version snapshot come exclusively from this
696	// organization's own live history; the version-zero and historical-policy
697	// judgment itself is shared with RecheckDecisionOffline in
698	// replayRecordedDecision.
699	func (s *Store) RecheckDecision(org string, seq int) (Decision, error) {
700		if org == "" {
701			return Decision{}, ErrMissingOrganization
702		}
703		if seq < 1 {
704			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, seq)
705		}
706		s.mu.Lock()
707		defer s.mu.Unlock()
708		st, ok := s.orgs[org]
709		if !ok || seq > len(st.audit) {
710			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: organization %q has no audit sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, org, seq)
711		}
712		rec := st.audit[seq-1]
713		if rec.Kind != AuditDecision || rec.Decision == nil {
714			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d is %s", ErrAuditNotADecision, seq, rec.Kind)
715		}
716		req := rec.Decision.Request
717		version := rec.Decision.Decision.Version
718		resolve := func(version int) versionPolicies {
719			src, ok := st.versions[version]
720			if !ok {
721				// A decision's version is immutable and never deleted; its
722				// absence indicates store tampering rather than normal
723				// operation.
724				return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAbsent}
725			}
726			// Live snapshots are immutable; detach anyway so the returned
727			// decision can never share storage with the store.
728			return versionPolicies{policies: append([]Policy(nil), src...)}
729		}
730		d, status := replayRecordedDecision(org, req, version, resolve)
731		if status == replayVersionAbsent {
732			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: decision used version %d, which no longer exists", ErrVersionNotFound, version)
733		}
734		return d, nil
735	}

1	// This file implements offline review of a single audited decision. It
2	// works solely from exported audit material: the complete record export,
3	// the separately retained checkpoint, and a target sequence. No Store is
4	// created or restored, so an organization can confirm why an access was
5	// allowed or denied long after the service instance that decided it has
6	// ended.
7	//
8	// The complete input must first validate as an audit chain. The policy
9	// version a decision actually used is recovered exclusively from policy
10	// change records preceding that decision within the same organization's
11	// export; later publishes or rollbacks, and a wider later export, cannot
12	// change the recomputed result.
13	package darksafe
14	
15	import "fmt"
16	
17	// OfflineDecisionReview compares the decision stored in an audited record
18	// with a decision recomputed purely from the exported material.
19	type OfflineDecisionReview struct {
20		// Seq is the reviewed decision record's sequence.
21		Seq int
22		// Original is the decision preserved in the audited record.
23		Original Decision
24		// Recomputed is the decision evaluated again offline from the saved
25		// request and the policy version it originally used.
26		Recomputed Decision
27		// Consistent reports whether both decisions agree on every field
28		// (allowance, reason, matched policies and version), treating a nil
29		// matched list and an empty matched list as the same.
30		Consistent bool
31	}
32	
33	// RecheckDecisionOffline re-evaluates one decision record offline. org is
34	// the organization name, records is its complete export starting at
35	// sequence 1 (a valid prefix is sufficient when paired with its own
36	// checkpoint), cp is the separately saved checkpoint, and seq identifies
37	// the decision record to review. The call is read-only: it neither mutates
38	// the supplied material nor appends audit records, and the returned
39	// decisions are detached from the input slices.
40	//
41	// The entire export is chain-validated before any result is produced;
42	// tampering anywhere, including in records after the target, fails the
43	// review. Distinguishable errors follow the other audit entry points:
44	// ErrMissingOrganization for an empty organization, ErrAuditNotFound for a
45	// non-positive or absent target sequence, and ErrAuditNotADecision when the
46	// target is a policy change record. When the saved decision names a
47	// policy version whose full content has no change record before the
48	// target, ErrVersionNotFound is returned; a newer version is never
49	// substituted, and a request the envelope would reject never masks the
50	// missing version.
51	//
52	// The fingerprint only proves the material matches its checkpoint; it
53	// cannot stand in for evaluating the request itself. So even when the
54	// declared version exists and carries an otherwise matching allow policy,
55	// the recomputation enforces the same request rules as the online
56	// decision: a disabled subject, an organization mismatch, a missing
57	// subject or resource organization or identifier, an empty action, and an
58	// illegal resource scope all deny, with the same reasons and precedence as
59	// Decide. Such a rejection uses no policies, so the recomputed decision
60	// reports version 0 with no matched policies; it is then compared field by
61	// field with the preserved original and may come back inconsistent.
62	func RecheckDecisionOffline(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint, seq int) (OfflineDecisionReview, error) {
63		if org == "" {
64			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, ErrMissingOrganization
65		}
66		// Validate the whole export first. A subject-filtered page, a fragment
67		// missing the beginning, or a checkpoint that does not pin the records
68		// all fail here, as does any corruption after the target.
69		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {
70			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, err
71		}
72		if seq < 1 {
73			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, seq)
74		}
75		if seq > len(records) {
76			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: export ends at %d, no sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, len(records), seq)
77		}
78		rec := &records[seq-1]
79		if rec.Kind != AuditDecision || rec.Decision == nil {
80			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d is %s", ErrAuditNotADecision, seq, rec.Kind)
81		}
82	
83		original := cloneDecisionValue(rec.Decision.Decision)
84		req := rec.Decision.Request
85		// Detach the request list by non-nil rather than by length: a non-nil
86		// empty role list with spare capacity must not be shared back with the
87		// caller's material, even though evaluation never reads any element.
88		req.Subject.Roles = cloneStrings(req.Subject.Roles)
89		version := original.Version
90	
91		// The version's full content must travel in a same-organization policy
92		// change record positioned before the decision. The replay core resolves
93		// the version before replaying any request rule, so a request the
94		// envelope rejects cannot mask a missing or later-only version.
95		resolve := func(want int) versionPolicies {
96			if policies, found := policiesBefore(records, seq-1, want); found {
97				return versionPolicies{policies: policies}
98			}
99			if _, later := policiesBefore(records, len(records), want); later {
100				return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAfterTarget}
101			}
102			return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAbsent}
103		}
104		recomputed, status := replayRecordedDecision(org, req, version, resolve)
105		switch status {
106		case replayVersionAfterTarget:
107			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf(
108				"%w: decision at sequence %d used version %d, whose change record appears only after it",
109				ErrVersionNotFound, seq, version)
110		case replayVersionAbsent:
111			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf(
112				"%w: decision at sequence %d used version %d, which has no policy change record in the export",
113				ErrVersionNotFound, seq, version)
114		}
115	
116		return OfflineDecisionReview{
117			Seq:        seq,
118			Original:   original,
119			Recomputed: recomputed,
120			Consistent: decisionsEqual(original, recomputed),
121		}, nil
122	}
123	
124	// policiesBefore searches records[:limit] for the policy change record that
125	// published version and returns a detached copy of its full content. The
126	// gapless chain validation guarantees records are in sequence order.
127	func policiesBefore(records []AuditRecord, limit, version int) ([]Policy, bool) {
128		for i := 0; i < limit; i++ {
129			r := &records[i]
130			if r.Kind != AuditPolicyChange || r.Change == nil {
131				continue
132			}
133			if r.Change.Version == version {
134				return append([]Policy(nil), r.Change.Policies...), true
135			}
136		}
137		return nil, false
138	}
139	
140	// cloneDecisionValue returns a decision detached from the input's matched
141	// slice. The list is detached whenever it is non-nil, including a non-nil
142	// empty list that still has spare capacity, so an append by one receiver
143	// can never reach another copy.
144	func cloneDecisionValue(d Decision) Decision {
145		d.Matched = cloneStrings(d.Matched)
146		return d
147	}
148	
149	// decisionsEqual compares every decision field. A nil matched list and an
150	// empty matched list describe the same set of hits.
151	func decisionsEqual(a, b Decision) bool {
152		if a.Allowed != b.Allowed || a.Reason != b.Reason || a.Version != b.Version {
153			return false
154		}
155		if len(a.Matched) == 0 && len(b.Matched) == 0 {
156			return true
157		}
158		if len(a.Matched) != len(b.Matched) {
159			return false
160		}
161		for i := range a.Matched {
162			if a.Matched[i] != b.Matched[i] {
163				return false
164			}
165		}
166		return true
167	}

1	// This file implements organization-scoped policy publishing, rollback,
2	// and review on top of the decision core. Each organization versions its
3	// own policy set independently; all state is in-memory and lives until
4	// the service instance ends.
5	package darksafe
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"sync"
13	)
14	
15	// Effect is the outcome a policy produces when it matches a request.
16	type Effect string
17	
18	const (
19		EffectAllow Effect = "allow"
20		EffectDeny  Effect = "deny"
21	)
22	
23	// Policy binds one subject and one action to a scope with an effect.
24	type Policy struct {
25		ID        string
26		Subject   string
27		Action    string
28		Scope     string
29		Effect    Effect
30		Recursive bool // false: only the exact scope; true: the scope and its descendants
31		// ResourceID optionally narrows the policy to one exact resource. Empty
32		// keeps the legacy scope-only matching. A non-empty value adds a
33		// condition on top of subject, action, scope and the organization
34		// checks: it never replaces them. Comparison is against the request's
35		// raw resource ID, byte for byte: case sensitive, spaces significant,
36		// no wildcard or scope-path interpretation, and the resource needs no
37		// prior registration.
38		//
39		// The omitempty tag is load bearing for audit fingerprints: the legacy
40		// JSON fingerprint family never had this field, and an empty value must
41		// keep serializing to exactly the old bytes.
42		ResourceID string `json:",omitempty"`
43	}
44	
45	// Sentinel errors so callers can distinguish failure causes with errors.Is.
46	var (
47		// ErrVersionConflict means the caller's expected current version is stale.
48		ErrVersionConflict = errors.New("darksafe: version conflict")
49		// ErrVersionNotFound means the requested historical version does not exist.
50		ErrVersionNotFound = errors.New("darksafe: version not found")
51		// ErrInvalidPolicySet means the submitted policy set failed validation.
52		ErrInvalidPolicySet = errors.New("darksafe: invalid policy set")
53		// ErrMissingOrganization means an operation was called without an organization.
54		ErrMissingOrganization = errors.New("darksafe: organization is required")
55	)
56	
57	// OrgRequest is an access request evaluated against one organization's
58	// published policies. Both organizations must equal the decision organization.
59	type OrgRequest struct {
60		SubjectOrg  string
61		ResourceOrg string
62		Subject     Subject
63		Resource    Resource
64		Action      string
65	}
66	
67	// Store holds every organization's published policy versions. It is safe
68	// for concurrent use and keeps all state in memory.
69	type Store struct {
70		mu   sync.Mutex
71		orgs map[string]*orgState
72	}
73	
74	type orgState struct {
75		current  int              // 0 means nothing published yet
76		versions map[int][]Policy // immutable snapshots per version
77		audit    []*AuditRecord   // gapless, append-only audit chain
78	}
79	
80	// NewStore returns an empty Store.
81	func NewStore() *Store {
82		return &Store{orgs: make(map[string]*orgState)}
83	}
84	
85	func (s *Store) orgLocked(name string) *orgState {
86		st, ok := s.orgs[name]
87		if !ok {
88			st = &orgState{versions: make(map[int][]Policy)}
89			s.orgs[name] = st
90		}
91		return st
92	}
93	
94	// CurrentVersion reports the organization's current version, 0 if it has
95	// never published.
96	func (s *Store) CurrentVersion(org string) int {
97		s.mu.Lock()
98		defer s.mu.Unlock()
99		if st, ok := s.orgs[org]; ok {
100			return st.current
101		}
102		return 0
103	}
104	
105	// Publish validates and publishes a complete policy set as the next
106	// version. expectedVersion must equal the organization's current version;
107	// on any validation or version failure nothing changes and no version
108	// number is consumed.
109	func (s *Store) Publish(org string, expectedVersion int, policies []Policy) (int, error) {
110		if org == "" {
111			return 0, ErrMissingOrganization
112		}
113		snapshot, err := validatePolicies(policies)
114		if err != nil {
115			return 0, err
116		}
117		s.mu.Lock()
118		defer s.mu.Unlock()
119		st := s.orgLocked(org)
120		if expectedVersion != st.current {
121			return 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: expected %d, current is %d", ErrVersionConflict, expectedVersion, st.current)
122		}
123		return st.commitVersionLocked(org, snapshot, 0, false), nil
124	}
125	
126	// Rollback republishes the full content of an existing historical version
127	// as a new version. History is never deleted or rewritten.
128	func (s *Store) Rollback(org string, expectedVersion, targetVersion int) (int, error) {
129		if org == "" {
130			return 0, ErrMissingOrganization
131		}
132		s.mu.Lock()
133		defer s.mu.Unlock()
134		st := s.orgLocked(org)
135		src, ok := st.versions[targetVersion]
136		if !ok {
137			return 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: organization %q has no version %d", ErrVersionNotFound, org, targetVersion)
138		}
139		if expectedVersion != st.current {
140			return 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: expected %d, current is %d", ErrVersionConflict, expectedVersion, st.current)
141		}
142		snapshot := append([]Policy(nil), src...)
143		return st.commitVersionLocked(org, snapshot, targetVersion, true), nil
144	}
145	
146	// commitVersionLocked advances the organization to the next version with
147	// the given policy snapshot and appends the matching policy-change record
148	// to the audit chain. It runs under the store mutex, so the new version
149	// and its audit record become visible together; callers must have already
150	// validated the input and checked the expected version, so a failed
151	// operation never reaches this point and leaves no record. A rollback
152	// passes its source version and rolledBack=true; an ordinary publish
153	// passes 0 and false.
154	func (st *orgState) commitVersionLocked(org string, snapshot []Policy, sourceVersion int, rolledBack bool) int {
155		st.current++
156		st.versions[st.current] = snapshot
157		st.appendAuditLocked(org, AuditPolicyChange, &PolicyChange{
158			Version:       st.current,
159			Policies:      snapshot,
160			SourceVersion: sourceVersion,
161			RolledBack:    rolledBack,
162		}, nil)
163		return st.current
164	}
165	
166	// Policies returns a copy of the full policy set of one version. Mutating
167	// the result does not affect published content.
168	func (s *Store) Policies(org string, version int) ([]Policy, error) {
169		s.mu.Lock()
170		defer s.mu.Unlock()
171		st, ok := s.orgs[org]
172		if !ok {
173			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: organization %q has no version %d", ErrVersionNotFound, org, version)
174		}
175		src, ok := st.versions[version]
176		if !ok {
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: organization %q has no version %d", ErrVersionNotFound, org, version)
178		}
179		return append([]Policy(nil), src...), nil
180	}
